domain: Institutional Design / International Relations / Political Economy
topic_summary: Analysis of the EU Council's unanimity voting requirement for foreign policy decisions as a contested institutional kernel. The same rule is read as either a sovereignty-preserving coordination mechanism or as a structural veto-trap enabling minoritarian extraction. Each reading instantiates fundamentally different constraint structures with different beneficiary/victim sets.

key_entities: EU Council unanimity rule (Article 31 TEU - foreign policy voting requirement)
Member states (27 sovereign entities with veto power)
European External Action Service (EEAS - foreign policy coordination body)
Blocking minorities (states using veto for extraction)
Coalition of the willing (subset proposing policy shift)
key_tensions: Sovereignty preservation vs collective action capacity (unanimity as protection vs paralysis)
Majoritarian preference vs minoritarian veto (policy preferred by 26 states blocked by 1)
key_mechanisms: Unanimity requirement enforcement (formal veto power at Council vote)
Opt-out extraction (threatening veto to extract concessions/side-payments)
Constructive abstention (allows policy to proceed without blocking while opting out)
key_absences: Formal accountability mechanism for veto use (no requirement to justify blocking)
Graduated escalation pathway (no institutional mechanism to override persistent blocking)

axes.human_readable: Unanimity as Sovereignty Guarantor (Essential Protection Against Coercion)
axes.structural_delta: Unanimity requirement interpreted as foundational safeguard preventing larger states from imposing foreign policy on smaller members
axes.primary_observable: Veto invocations framed as legitimate sovereignty defense; public discourse treating unanimity as non-negotiable principle
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel - instantiates unanimity as coordination mechanism protecting against majoritarian extraction

axes.structural_delta: Unanimity requirement interpreted as structural vulnerability enabling single states to extract concessions by threatening to block collective preference
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of policy blockage by minority; correlation between veto threats and side-payment extraction; foreign policy paralysis metrics
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel - instantiates unanimity as extraction mechanism with inverted beneficiary structure

axes.human_readable: Unanimity as Diplomatic Capital Allocation (Consensus-Building Norm)
axes.structural_delta: Unanimity requirement interpreted as forcing iterative consensus-building that strengthens legitimacy and commitment to adopted policies
axes.primary_observable: Policy implementation compliance rates; diplomatic negotiation duration before votes; post-adoption defection frequency
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel - captures consensus-building interpretation distinct from sovereignty/extraction binary

axes.human_readable: Unanimity as Geopolitical Impotence (External Actor Exploitation)
axes.structural_delta: Unanimity requirement interpreted as making EU systematically vulnerable to external actors who can block collective response by capturing single member state
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of third-party influence over individual member vetos; correlation between external pressure and policy blockage; geopolitical response latency
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: fourth reading exceeds three-axis budget; captured indirectly through veto_trap_reading's extraction mechanics plus omega on external capture

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Unanimity as external actor exploitation pathway via single-state capture
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Fourth reading exceeds three-axis budget; external capture dimension partially covered by veto_trap_reading mechanics; omega generated for external influence pathway

omegas.description: Does external actor influence over individual member states constitute a distinct reading of unanimity, or is it a downstream consequence of the veto-trap reading? If Russia/China can reliably block EU sanctions through captured proxies, unanimity becomes snare with non-member beneficiary.
omegas.source: Deferred axis geopolitical_impotence_reading + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Constructive abstention (Article 31 TEU) allows policy to proceed despite objection. Does this mechanism's existence invalidate the 'pure veto-trap' reading, or does its limited use confirm the sovereignty_guarantor reading's dominance in practice?
omegas.source: Extraction mechanism inventory - escape valve not fully explored in any reading

omegas.description: Do readings converge or diverge under acute crisis? Ukraine invasion context: did unanimity enable rapid sanctions coordination (sovereignty_guarantor wins) or did Hungary's blocking behavior vindicate veto_trap reading? Observational data post-2022 may adjudicate.
omegas.source: F15 Premature Closure check - temporal variation in reading dominance not captured

omegas.description: If Treaty reform expands qualified majority voting to foreign policy domains, which reading predicted the reform's necessity? The push for QMV expansion is itself evidence for veto_trap reading's validity, but sovereignty_guarantor reading frames it as illegitimate sovereignty erosion.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) - reform debate is meta-evidence about which reading holds in practice

fracture_scan.notes: F15 detected: temporal dimension underexplored - reading dominance may shift with geopolitical context (pre/post Ukraine invasion, enlargement dynamics). Generated omega_reading_stability_under_crisis to bound this uncertainty. All three readings remain structurally valid as interpretive commitments.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Article 31 TEU unanimity requirement for Common Foreign and Security Policy decisions - the stabilized procedural rule that all parties must adjudicate their claims through
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Treaty text as interpreted through Council practice and ECJ jurisprudence; member states claim authority to read unanimity principle through national sovereignty lens vs supranational effectiveness lens
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Consensus Trap (Type 5) - authority is diffused across all member states equally; revision requires unanimity to change unanimity

readings.commitment: Unanimity as foundational protection against majoritarian coercion - each state must consent to collective action that implicates sovereignty
readings.authority_grounding: Westphalian sovereignty norm; Treaty founders' intent to preserve member state autonomy; constitutional traditions of smaller states
readings.expected_structural_delta: Veto use is legitimate sovereignty defense; beneficiary set = all small states; no extraction - blocking is rights-exercise. ε moderate because coordination costs exist but no systematic extraction occurs.

readings.commitment: Unanimity as structural vulnerability enabling minoritarian extraction through credible blocking threats
readings.authority_grounding: Collective action theory; observed patterns of side-payment extraction; supranational efficiency norm
readings.expected_structural_delta: Veto use is extraction mechanism; beneficiary = blocking state; victim = coalition majority. High ε because blocking systematically transfers value from majority preference to minority position through concessions/opt-outs.

readings.commitment: Unanimity as consensus-building requirement that forces iterative negotiation and strengthens policy legitimacy
readings.authority_grounding: Deliberative democracy theory; EU's historical consensus culture; diplomatic practice norms
readings.expected_structural_delta: Unanimity is coordination cost with legitimacy payoff; no fixed beneficiary/victim structure. Low ε because while negotiation is costly, it produces buy-in that reduces downstream defection. Unanimous decisions more durable than QMV impositions.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Sovereignty_guarantor treats veto as legitimate rights-exercise (no extraction occurs); veto_trap treats identical veto as extraction mechanism (value transfer from majority to minority). No single framework can hold both: either blocking is rights-protection OR it is extraction, not both simultaneously. The empirical act is the same; the normative classification is mutually exclusive.
